covers: Held-out story where the point is about someone else's advice being wrong — an easy place for a model to editorialise beyond the idea.
idea: Story about the coach I quit after six weeks because every session ended with him telling me I needed to want it more, and how the next coach just changed my rest times and my sleep and the problem went away.

sections.text: I did not need to want it more. I needed to sleep.
Six weeks with a coach whose answer to every bad session was that I wanted it less than the people getting results.

So I quit, which took me longer than it should have. The next coach asked what my rest times were and what time I was getting to bed. He made the rest longer, moved the sessions earlier, and they stopped falling apart halfway through. Same body, same effort, different inputs.
If effort had been the problem, more effort would have fixed it. It never did.
If every session ends with you being told to try harder, ask what else changed. If the answer is nothing, leave.

voice_fidelity.evidence: Blunt about someone else without hyping the outcome, and the close is one line in the profile's register.

hook_distinctiveness.evidence: Four distinct promises, though the contrarian hook and the payoff make the same move twice.

script_completeness.evidence: The body names both changes and the close gives the viewer a decision rule to act on.

instruction_adherence.evidence: Only rest times and sleep are named as the fix — no coaching credential, method or research is introduced.
